items.title: Set up the app and handle quantities correctly
items.scope: Create the mobile project and make quantity input reliable.
acceptance: Accept decimal points or commas for decimal units.
Allow only whole numbers for units such as cartons.
Round to three decimal places; ask the user if a positive amount rounds to zero.

items.title: Track what is needed and what was bought
items.scope: Keep shopping needs and individual purchases separate.
acceptance: Purchases by different people add together; retrying a save never counts twice.
Undoing a purchase keeps the requested amount unchanged.
A new shopping need is not fulfilled by purchases from an earlier one.

items.title: Keep offline changes safe after closing the app
items.scope: Save shopping changes and the work waiting to sync together.
acceptance: Closing or crashing the app does not lose a saved purchase.
Retrying a save does not create a duplicate.
One account cannot see another account’s saved data.

items.title: Build the first offline shopping screen
items.scope: Create a development version to try the basic shopping flow.
acceptance: Add an item, edit its amount, buy the remaining amount or enter an amount manually, and undo a purchase.
The list survives restarting the app; purchased items appear in a collapsed section at the bottom.
The screen clearly shows unsynced changes; test accounts are unavailable in release builds.

items.title: Choose a sign-in service
items.scope: Check which hosted sign-in service supports our approved account rules.
acceptance: Email codes and an optional password work for the same account.
Email changes, password recovery, account deletion and signing out other devices are supported.
Record costs and limitations before choosing a provider; paid services need separate approval.

items.title: Add sign-in and protect saved account data
items.scope: Connect real accounts and keep each person’s local data private.
acceptance: Previously signed-in users can keep working offline.
Signing out hides saved data and warns about unsynced changes.
Revoked access is enforced when the app reconnects; a new account cannot inherit an old account’s data.

items.title: Create households and invite members
items.scope: Let people create a household, invite others and manage membership.
acceptance: Household creation offers an empty or starter catalog and an empty Shopping list.
Invitations work once, expire after seven days and require an explicit Join action.
Leaving, removal, owner succession and unassigned shopping needs follow the approved rules.

items.title: Define how offline changes are exchanged
items.scope: Write the shared rules that the app and server use to exchange changes.
acceptance: Every change can be retried safely and tied to the action it depends on.
Old offline work can reconnect without losing valid changes or restoring permanently deleted data.
Examples cover conflicts, shopping cycles and the approved D1–D7 decisions.

items.title: Save shared changes safely on the server
items.scope: Build the server foundation for accepting household changes.
acceptance: Only current household members can read or change its data.
A repeated request has only one effect.
Each accepted change and its result are saved together, and clients can retrieve every accepted change.

items.title: Sync phones after working offline
items.scope: Send pending changes and download shared updates when a connection returns.
acceptance: Retries and interrupted connections do not lose or duplicate purchases.
Phones catch up after a long absence while preserving valid offline work.
The app shows successful sync only after the server confirms it.

items.title: Resolve conflicts without losing shopping intent
items.scope: Apply the agreed rules when people change the same shopping data.
acceptance: Quantity conflicts follow the household setting; independent purchases still add together.
Unclear old-versus-new shopping needs ask whether to merge or keep separate.
Manual choices, competing corrections and undo follow the approved rules.

items.title: Reuse products and prevent duplicates
items.scope: Help people choose existing household products before creating new ones.
acceptance: Check existing products and suggest similar matches.
Merge or keep separate using the approved choices; preserve units and purchase history.
Retired products and reused names do not overwrite older records.

items.title: Support useful units and custom units
items.scope: Support whole-number and decimal measures, including household-created units.
acceptance: Users can create units; the default is whole numbers.
Only combine units representing the same measure and scale, with confirmation where needed.
Conflicting unit edits preserve purchases and ask for correction without silently converting amounts.

items.title: Add multiple lists, buyers and notes
items.scope: Complete the everyday list views and editing features.
acceptance: Support multiple lists, common and grouped views, and remembered view preferences.
New items are assigned to their creator; ordinary edits preserve the buyer.
Merged or conflicting notes preserve the agreed text; name conflicts never discard contents.

items.title: Delete and restore lists and items correctly
items.scope: Apply the agreed deletion, restoration and permanent-deletion rules.
acceptance: Deletion conflicts are reported; purchases can keep an item visible as agreed.
Undoing such a purchase does not silently hide the item again.
Restoring old purchases does not satisfy new demand; permanent list deletion cannot be undone by old offline work.

items.title: Show useful in-app notices and push alerts
items.scope: Tell the right people about conflicts without unnecessary alerts.
acceptance: Use the approved recipients and channels; in-app-only events never become push alerts.
Reading a notice does not resolve an outstanding choice.
Group related alerts and handle delivery retries without relying on push for synchronization.

items.title: Handle account deletion and lost access
items.scope: Remove access and personal information according to the approved rules.
acceptance: Account deletion requires fresh verification and preserves other members’ shared history as Deleted member.
Closing the last membership removes the household; removed users cannot export its data.
Document backup deletion and mailbox-recovery limits, and test that deleted data cannot return.

items.title: Test offline use and collaboration end to end
items.scope: Check the complete experience across devices and unreliable connections.
acceptance: Test crashes, retries, long offline periods and several people editing together.
Cover all approved conflict and deletion outcomes, including D1–D7.
Record actual device coverage and confirm that accounts and households stay isolated.

items.title: Prepare hosting and a beta release
items.scope: Prepare a concrete deployment and testing proposal when the app is ready.
acceptance: Confirm app name, platform accounts, test devices, beta audience and costs.
Plan hosting, backups, monitoring and recovery without disrupting existing services.
Get separate approval before deployment, signing or publication.
